newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea encourages its brokerages to go abroad.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea encourages its brokerages to go abroad.

text.p: South Korea's Finance Ministry will make it easier for domestic brokerages to expand overseas, Yonhap news agency reported on Sunday.

Yonhap quoted the Finance Ministry as saying brokerages could set up wholly-owned subsidiaries, joint ventures and branch offices if they maintained sound business records. It gave no timetable for the move.
Officials at the ministry were unavailable for comment.
Yonhap said securities firms would also be permitted to open overseas liaison offices from next April by simply reporting to the ministry.
Currently, brokerages need ministry approval to open an overseas liaison office.
The ministry said the number of new overseas outlets, excluding liaison offices, permitted for any brokerage house would be limited to two each year to ensure a "stable and gradual" advance.
A rule requiring securities houses to open a liaison office for a minimum of one year before setting up overseas' outlets would be scrapped.
